title: Choose Tukar's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Balikbayan Parcel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Balikbayan Parcel
options.lineage: the box a migrant worker packs and sends home: kraft corrugate, packing tape, stencil, shipping label, customs stamp
options.thesis: A remittance is a sealed parcel: nobody on the road can see what is inside, yet every box carries a label the customs desk can stamp. Refuses the fintech phone-mockup hero and the crypto glow.
options.viewport: The whole first viewport is the top of one sealed box seen from above. A large white shipping label carries TUKAR in stencil, the fields FROM and TO deliberately blacked out, CONTENTS: 'USDC, amount sealed', and a fresh blue customs stamp 'COMPLIANCE CLEARED, proof on-chain'. The primary action 'Send a box home' sits on the label as the courier's tear-off stub; 'Open a box' is the second stub. A routing strip of corridor codes (ID PH MX BR AR VN TH IN NG CO) runs as tape along the bottom edge.
options.risk: Can read as e-commerce logistics instead of money if the label copy drifts; cardboard texture overdone turns kitsch. Held by the three-ink rule and label-grade typography.

raised.raise: Three permitted inks only (stencil black, tape red, stamp blue) on kraft; no fourth color anywhere, on any surface.
One small landmark mark, the tape-seal glyph, appears exactly once on every view, where the eye lands last.
Every amount is set in fixed-position stencil digits, tabular, so a changing number is a physical event, never a reflow.
One shared motion clock: tape unrolls, stamps land, and stubs tear at the same tempo across all surfaces.

options.label: Security Print
options.lineage: banknote engraving: guilloche, intaglio, watermark, security thread, serial numbers
options.thesis: Money that carries its own proof: the note is private in your pocket and verifiable under a lamp. Watermark = shielded amount, thread = on-chain proof, serial = commitment.
options.viewport: A banknote-proportioned hero: the product name as the engraved denomination, a watermark region that only reveals the amount when 'held to the light' (hover/press), a security thread that runs the whole page as the proof rail, serial numbers as commitments.
options.risk: Familiar: guilloche and engraved money is where most fintech brand work lands; it is my top-ranked grounded direction precisely because it is the obvious fit.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: a silk cape with hidden drawcord channels; one pull turns a flat plane into a protective volume
options.thesis: One pull shields the money: the flat public plane gathers into a private volume, then relaxes at the other end.
options.viewport: A black semicircle plane; pulling the gold cord (scroll or drag) gathers it into pleats around the amount, which becomes unreadable; a second pull releases it at the receiver.
options.case: Dramatizes the shielding mechanism better than any grounded candidate, but migrant workers do not identify with couture silk, and the black ground sits next to the banned dark look.
options.risk: Reads as fashion, and black silk drifts toward the anti-reference.

options.label: Exposed Binding
options.lineage: coptic-bound book with chain stitching running outside the spine; the structure is the only ornament
options.thesis: Nothing is hidden: the thread that holds the ledger together runs on the outside, so compliance is visible structure, not a claim.
options.viewport: A spine of chain-stitch links, one per corridor or proof, generated live from real on-chain counts; opening a section lays it flat.
options.case: Carries 'provable compliance' with structural honesty; loses on audience identification (handmade books are far from the remittance counter) and its cream paper is my known default.
options.risk: Cream paper plus craft is the rendition this category of brief keeps landing on.

options.label: Socialist Kiosk Print
options.lineage: state kiosk goods printed in three permitted inks with a central office mark
options.case: A goods grid does not map to sending money home, and the audience does not identify with state print.

options.label: Magazine Program
options.lineage: mid-century magazine identity with one hidden silhouette mark per cover
options.case: Editorial two-column reading is the wrong mode for a Persuade landing and a phone-first sender; no audience identification.
options.kept: One small landmark mark on every view.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.lineage: laboratory counter with orange plasma digits in glass tubes
options.case: Orange glow on black is exactly the incumbent look and the banned crypto glow.
options.kept: Amounts in fixed digit positions, a change as a physical event.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.lineage: demo-scene title screen: bitmap text over an emissive black void, depth as rank
options.case: Black void plus amber caret is the banned terminal look, and depth-as-rank does not explain a remittance.
options.kept: One shared motion clock for the whole surface.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The remittance app landing everyone ships: white ground, navy and one accent, a phone mockup, three benefit cards, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, phone mockup right, trust row of logos below (we have none to show, so proof would be the explorer links).
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Wise, Remitly, and every fintech template; the honest-proof story has nowhere to live.
